literature_claim_statement: Digital Twin technology is an established paradigm for predictive maintenance and condition monitoring across Industry 4.0 and civil infrastructure.
source_title: A Survey on AI-Driven Digital Twins in Industry 4.0: Smart Manufacturing and Advanced Robotics
notes_and_context: Supported additionally by Hasan & Crawford (2025, Digital Twin), Pathri & Ganduri (2025), and Wei (2024 NTU thesis). Proves DT + PdM is not a novel concept.

claim_topic: RUL point prediction on C-MAPSS is mature
literature_claim_statement: Point estimation of turbofan Remaining Useful Life on the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark using machine learning and deep learning is mature and heavily published.
source_title: Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation
exact_citation_location: IEEE PHM 2008, pp. 1-9; Wu et al. (2026, Sensors 26(4), p. 2)
notes_and_context: C-MAPSS benchmark was formulated in 2008. Over 500+ papers benchmark point RUL. GA-stacking ensemble achieves 13.82 RMSE in Wu et al. (2026). Point prediction alone has zero novelty.

claim_topic: Digital Twin directly integrated with C-MAPSS RUL
literature_claim_statement: Coupling a Digital Twin software architecture with machine learning RUL estimation on NASA C-MAPSS telemetry has already been demonstrated in peer-reviewed literature.
source_title: Research on Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Equipment Based on Digital Twins
notes_and_context: Wu et al. (2026) directly implement a 4-tier Digital Twin framework that streams C-MAPSS FD001 telemetry into an ensemble RUL predictor. Disproves that 'DT + C-MAPSS RUL' is novel.

literature_claim_statement: Prognostic models generating prediction intervals or probabilistic distributions rather than deterministic point estimates are well-documented in reliability literature.
source_title: Data-driven predictive maintenance strategy considering the uncertainty in remaining useful life prediction
notes_and_context: Supported additionally by Walia & Kumar (2026, RESS), Zhu et al. (2025, QREI), and Xu et al. (2026, RESS). Uncertainty estimation in RUL is an established research direction.

claim_topic: RUL uncertainty connected to maintenance decisions
literature_claim_statement: Integrating RUL uncertainty into predictive maintenance decisions and cost optimization models has already been formulated and validated.
source_title: Data-driven predictive maintenance strategy considering the uncertainty in remaining useful life prediction
notes_and_context: Chen et al. (2022) formulate an expected cost-rate maintenance policy under RUL uncertainty on C-MAPSS; Zhu et al. (2025) formulate prediction-interval replacement thresholds; Walia & Kumar (2026) use RL maintenance scheduling. Disproves novelty of 'uncertainty + maintenance decisions'.

claim_topic: Conformal calibration has been applied to C-MAPSS
literature_claim_statement: Inductive split conformal prediction has already been successfully applied to deep neural networks on NASA C-MAPSS datasets to guarantee marginal prediction interval coverage.
source_title: Conformal Prediction Intervals for Remaining Useful Lifetime Estimation
notes_and_context: Javanmardi & Hüllermeier (2023) and Diao et al. (2026) demonstrated split conformal prediction on C-MAPSS, achieving nominal marginal coverage (90% and 95%). Disproves novelty of 'conformal prediction on C-MAPSS'.

claim_topic: Stage-wise interval behavior has been observed
literature_claim_statement: Prediction interval widths naturally contract as an engineering asset advances through degradation stages toward end-of-life.
source_title: Conformal Prediction Intervals for Remaining Useful Lifetime Estimation
exact_citation_location: IJPHM 2023, 14(2), Figure 4-6; Walia & Kumar (2026, RESS 256, Figure 8)
notes_and_context: Normalized non-conformity scores and Bayesian variance both show interval shrinkage near failure; however, rigorous conditional coverage breakdown across discrete early/mid/late stages was not evaluated.

claim_topic: Operating-regime conditional reliability studied in rotating machinery
literature_claim_statement: Marginal calibration guarantees have been shown to hide severe conditional undercoverage when assets experience operating-regime shifts in bearing testbeds.
source_title: Empirical Calibration and Conditional-Reliability Diagnostics for Bearing RUL Prediction under Operating-Regime Shift
notes_and_context: Yang et al. (2026) show that 91% marginal coverage dropped to 64% in demanding operating regimes in bearing benchmarks; demonstrates conditional coverage vulnerability under distribution shift.

claim_topic: Downstream decision effects of conditional miscalibration underexplored
literature_claim_statement: An underexplored intersection appears to be the relationship between conditional RUL calibration failures across degradation stages and operating regimes and their measurable downstream maintenance-decision consequences.
source_title: Turbofan Engine Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Reliable Prediction Intervals via LSTM-Based Quantile Regression and Conformal Calibration
exact_citation_location: Sensors 2026, 26(7), 2249, Discussion Section; Xu et al. (2026, RESS 257, Section 6)
evidence_type: Systematic Gap Synthesis Across Closest Works
notes_and_context: Conformal RUL papers (Diao 2026, Javanmardi 2023, Xu 2026) evaluate only statistical coverage (PICP/ECE) and ignore maintenance decisions. Maintenance decision papers (Chen 2022, Walia 2026) rely on uncalibrated parametric or heuristic uncertainty. The direct causal mapping from conditional miscalibration to operational maintenance loss remains unmeasured.
